hero.lead: A nation of 4.6 million joining two oceans, with forest across six tenths of its land and seven tenths of its power renewable, where the World Bank supports fiscal sustainability and a modern land registry.

capital.heading: The crossroads of two oceans, and a nation of readers.

register.name: Global Bonds due 2034 and 2038, with a repurchase of nine Global Bonds
register.detail: Ministry of Economy and Finance · results announced 19 February 2026 · $1.49bn due 2034 at 5.227% · $1.49bn due 2038 at 5.662% · about $2.97bn of nine Global Bonds repurchased
register.note: Demand above $13bn; a net cut of about $204M in public debt and about $30M a year less in interest
register.text: Two dollar bonds sold on the international market in the first quarter of 2026, whose proceeds paid for the repurchase of about $2.97 billion of nine older Global Bonds. The Ministry of Economy and Finance reports a net cut of about $204 million in public debt and about $30 million a year less in interest, which leaves more of the budget for the seven standards.

register.name: National Multipurpose Cadastre Program-for-Results
register.detail: World Bank (IBRD) · approved by the Board, press release 29 April 2026 · P511840 · Program-for-Results · part of a $95.15M programme with Government of Panama resources · National Land Administration Authority (ANATI)
register.note: Only about 36% of the territory has cadastral information and 19% of properties are titled
register.text: An IBRD loan, disbursed against results, for a national multipurpose cadastre that brings land and property records onto one digital platform and improves cadastral and land tenure services in selected areas. Greater legal security over land serves the shelter and livelihood standards; the World Bank expects about 1,200 direct jobs during implementation.

register.name: Fiscal Management and Growth Development Policy Loan
register.detail: World Bank (IBRD) · approved by the Board December 2025 · 25 years with two years’ grace · disbursed in the first quarter of 2026 (Ministry of Economy and Finance)
register.note: Reforms to the Fiscal Responsibility Law, the pension system, tax administration and the local debt market
register.text: World Bank budget support for reforms that update the Fiscal Responsibility Law, strengthen the pension system, improve tax administration, develop the local debt market and ease public-private partnerships. It finances the public budget as a whole and the pension system that protects the livelihood of older Panamanians.

register.name: World Bank Group guarantees for a ten-year commercial loan
register.detail: IBRD policy-based guarantee of $600M, first loss · MIGA guarantee of up to $1,174M, second loss · together 95% of principal and interest · approved December 2025
register.note: The Ministry of Economy and Finance expects about $64.6M a year in interest savings
register.text: A ten-year commercial loan of up to $1.4 billion to the Government of Panama for general budgetary purposes, covered by a first-loss IBRD guarantee and a second-loss MIGA guarantee. The World Bank calls the combined guarantee model a financial innovation that could be replicated; cheaper refinancing leaves more room in the budget for the seven standards.

register.name: Second Climate Resilience and Green Growth DPL
register.text: Budget support for climate resilience and green growth.

register.name: A/B loan to Banco Nacional de Panamá for agriculture and SMEs in rural areas
register.detail: CAF · signing reported 14 September 2026 · borrower Banco Nacional de Panamá, the state bank · half for agribusiness and agro-industry, half for small and medium enterprises
register.note: About 3,300 small and medium enterprises, with emphasis on businesses led by women
register.text: A CAF loan to Banco Nacional de Panamá, half for agribusiness and agro-industry, mainly in rural areas, and half for small and medium enterprises, with green projects in energy efficiency and renewable energy. It serves the food and livelihood standards in the countryside.

register.name: Sanitation programme for Panama City, Arraiján and La Chorrera
register.detail: IDB · investment loan approved by the Board, reported 4 September 2026 · 18 years, 6.5 years’ grace, SOFR-based rate · first operation of a $210M Conditional Credit Line for Investment Projects
register.note: About 310,000 people to gain access to sanitation
register.text: An IDB loan to rehabilitate the Amador sewerage system, build the Caimito wastewater treatment plant, continue the Matansillo River main interceptor and train the Panama Sanitation Program Coordinating Unit. It also supports Panama’s Sustainable Financing Framework, and it serves the water and shelter standards.

register.name: Support Program for Efficiency and Equity in Panama’s Health System
register.detail: IDB · approved 22 July 2026 · 6163/OC-PN · first operation of a credit line of up to $120M over 12 years · $10M national counterpart, $50M in all
register.note: 514,000 people in 24 priority districts, where 60% of the population is Indigenous
register.text: An IDB loan to improve access to health services and financial protection in health: closer coordination between the Ministry of Health and the Social Security Fund, better medicine management, mobile and community health teams in Indigenous and rural areas and six resilient health centres. It serves the health standard in rural and Indigenous districts.

register.name: Program for the Improvement of the Social Security Fund Pension System
register.detail: IDB · approved 22 October 2025 · 6055/OC-PN · shown as closed by the IDB
register.note: The Disability, Old Age and Death (IVM) programme of the Social Security Fund
register.text: An IDB loan to improve the sustainability of the Disability, Old Age and Death programme run by the Social Security Fund, by strengthening its financing, widening its coverage and making retirement benefits more adequate. A sound pension system protects the livelihood of older Panamanians and the public finances that carry the seven standards.

register.name: Sustainable forest management loan
register.detail: CAF · approved 29 June 2025 · continuity of policies for sustainable forest management, ecosystem conservation and green financing
register.note: Forests regulate rainfall and help prevent floods and landslides
register.text: A CAF loan to Panama to improve forest management and support policies for sustainable forest management, ecosystem conservation and green financing, with responsible timber production, ecotourism and the bioeconomy. Forests that regulate rainfall and prevent floods and landslides bear on the water, shelter and livelihood standards.

register.name: Bringing clean energy to Panama’s most remote communities
register.detail: European Union contribution to a €61.4M programme with AECID, the IDB and the Government of Panama · project period 19 December 2019 to 31 August 2026 · Ngäbe Buglé region
register.note: More than 32,437 users, including households, 279 schools and 103 health facilities
register.text: A European Union contribution to rural electrification in Panama with the Spanish Agency for International Development Cooperation and the IDB: photovoltaic installations, mini-grids and grid extensions in the Ngäbe Buglé region, and stronger planning at the Rural Electrification Office. Clean power for homes, schools and health facilities serves the energy, education and health standards.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Power from water, wind and sun already flows; every new connection can be clean.

items.name: The Visitors
items.label: Of export earnings from visitors, 2020
items.text: Visitors already pay for the coast and the culture; their spending can finance what lasts.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 24.5% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: The Minerals
items.label: Of GDP from mineral rents, 2021
items.text: Metals and minerals already earn; the task is to keep more of their value at home.

items.name: Arukay
items.text: A Panama-based education company whose technology-based learning system equips Latin American students with problem-solving and soft skills, and which reports reaching more than 75,000 students in ten countries.

items.name: Silver Guardian
items.text: The first silver-economy mobile app in Panama, connecting older adults with preventive health, remote health monitoring and local businesses; the Betania project built on it, with more than 3,500 older adults in digital literacy and health telemonitoring programmes, won the top digital equity prize in the IDB’s tenth Gobernarte contest.

items.name: Microserfin
items.text: The Panamanian microfinance entity of the BBVA Microfinance Foundation, which offers adapted financing, technical support and training to more than 18,400 microentrepreneurs.
